answer.origin: Investing.com article published 2026-07-22, reporting BofA Research; the throughput figures are BofA’s characterization of AMD’s own estimates. The underlying estimate date and model materials are not stated.
answer.note: BofA says AMD estimates that, in a modeled 100kW rack deployment, EPYC 9965 (Turin) delivers about 2.4x the throughput of NVIDIA’s Vera baseline, and projects next-generation EPYC 6 (Venice) at about 3.3x. These are AMD-attributed model estimates relayed by BofA, not independent benchmark results or demonstrated customer deployments. For NVDA, they indicate a possible competitive challenge if AMD’s throughput and service-density framing proves relevant to buyers’ agentic-AI workloads; they do not establish that AMD is superior on other measures or that customers will choose it. The article says BofA frames Vera around latency, per-thread progress, GPU utilization, and an integrated AI system, versus AMD’s concurrency and throughput framing, and does not declare a winner. BofA also projects the server CPU TAM to reach $170 billion by 2030, roughly four times current levels; this is an analyst forecast and does not establish NVDA’s share or revenue. The article is dated 2026-07-22 and describes AMD’s AI 2026 Day as upcoming.
limitations: The underlying AMD model’s workload, hardware configuration, throughput definition, and other assumptions are not provided, limiting assessment of how comparable the modeled 100kW results are to real deployments.
No independent test results or customer adoption evidence are provided to show whether the claimed throughput advantage translates into buyer preference or NVDA business impact.
The basis for BofA’s $170 billion 2030 market forecast and its implications for NVDA’s addressable revenue or market share are not stated.
follow_up: Review AMD’s AI 2026 Day materials and the underlying model assumptions for the EPYC-versus-Vera 100kW comparison; check whether the workload, configuration, and throughput metric permit an apples-to-apples comparison.
Track subsequent independent benchmark disclosures and customer or hyperscaler deployment evidence for Vera and the cited EPYC products to test whether the modeled comparison affects adoption.
Check BofA’s research for the assumptions behind its $170 billion 2030 server CPU TAM forecast and any explicit estimate of NVDA’s exposure or share.
